properties.documentation:
Represents either manual or automatic alignment. It can be also used to represent uncertain automatic alignments.
Note: Uncertain automatic alignments will be used in the web curation app to show alternative alignments, but they'll never be used as a "primary" link provided for link curation.

documentation.value: This indicates a confidence of belonging to a cluster: 0 - 1 : automatically computed -1 : rejected by a person

properties.documentation:
The alignment link set is a collection of alignment links that form a set of possible alignments for the same entity. Usually the link set serves as a decision context defined by the alternative alignment links automatically derived. Then it is called a DecisionContext.
In addition, to make a decission in the UI, it is necessary to access the entity representation, and the canonical entities representations. Note: There is no distinction between the main (canonical) and alternative (potential) alignments. This is determined by the confidence score (link with the highest score links to the canonical entity). Optionally, the list can be sorted by score in descending order.
No two links can exist for the same entity mention within the entire store. The alignment links MUST be to distinct entity mentions.

The decision object captures what (integration) action shall be taken given a DeciusionContex.
Integration needed in 2 context * when a response comes from ERE , we need to (step 1) store the alternatives + (step 2) automatically accept the top alternative if it is above and (step 3) upsert it into the canonical entity registry *
* For automated actions ... * For user actions ...
The decision-making integration logic is as follows: 1) Accepting the automatic alignment * confidenceScore of the proposed alignment is left as is. 2) Reassigning the mention to another proposed entity * confidenceScore of the chosen alignment is set to 1.0 * confidenceScore of the proposed alignment is set to -1.0 * other alternative alignments are note affected 2) Rejecting the automatic alignment * confidenceScore of both proposed alignment and alternative alignments is set to -1.0

Stores data for * knowing the choice context * training machine learning models

properties.documentation:
This needs rethinking.
We always request and response to bulks of entity mentions/resolutions. And a bulk of ONE is also a bulk.
Make sure we have a simple way to returnign back the requestID, canonicalID.
We assume TED-SWS wille xtract the URI from the RDF payload, and use it as requestID in the first place.
Protocol: - ERS sends a resolution requect, for a single entity mention record - ERS responds with a single response object, that contains one ore more possible links to canonical URIs

Rebuild protocol - ERS sends a request to the ERE to rebuild the clusters - ERE starts rebuilding using the existent data - ERE sends back multiple responses each containing one canonical entity (canonical URI + all of the entity mentions);

Sync protocol: - ERS can ask ERE for the latest timestamp of entity mentions - ERS responds with a timestamp - ERE sends a feed of records that are newer than the timestamp.
Note 1: ERS can just start feeding ERE everything it has in the system of records, to be sure of the data completness. Note 2: (Otherwise) This is a simplified protocol, it does not cover the "lost" records (i.e. gaps in the data, e.g. a record is in the ERS but for some technical reason is lost in the ERE), which would require a through two way synch between ERE and ERS

We shall always have one record per resolution request. Do not make the mistake of including multiple records into one request.
Use bulk for that. Future optimisation.

documentation.value: This is a way to ensure that the governance of Canonical URIs stays with the ERS.

properties.documentation:
Supports one entity resolution or bulk resolution response.
One response with multiple possible assignments. WE shall use this option (not multiple responses for one request) because:- the ERE will always produce all the possible assignments at the same time, - it facilitates easier integration, on the ERS side, into the canonical registry.

This is a request to re-create the clusters within the ERE, given the current (cached) data.
It shall re-use the available cluster/canonical URIs, but the memberships may differ. Or possibly will provide new canonical URIs, which then will have to be accomodated by the ERS.

ERS requests fro the latest/newest entity mention known by the ERE.
This is determining the scope of data.
Initiated by the ERS, sending over the entity mention records, without expecting any resolutions in response.
